rules._schema: Parcel float allowlist — which observed windows auto-tiling leaves UNADOPTED (floating at natural z-order). Consumed by lib/jq/autotile.jq float_verdict/tileable. ORDERED, last-matching-rule-wins: a narrow manage:on rule declared AFTER a broad manage:off rule re-manages the exception. Each rule: { id, app?: <regex over the window's app name>, title?: <regex over the window's title>, manage: on|off }. An omitted app/title facet matches anything; a window with no matching rule defaults to manage:on (tiled). AGGRESSIVE POLICY (Phase B, 2026-05-30): the allowlist is deliberately NEAR-EMPTY — is_resizable + is_standard (the STRUCTURAL gate in tileable) are the real 'can it tile' filter; they already exclude non-resizable utilities, modal dialogs (AXDialog), sheets (AXSheet), floating panels (AXFloatingWindow), and overlays. This file is PURE PREFERENCE on top of that gate. We keep ONLY structurally-necessary entries: the WezTerm wm.surface.* pair (wm's OWN transient surfaces — manage:off, with the notes-panel manage:on override that MUST stay last) and Raycast (a borderless launcher overlay, belt-and-suspenders even though is_standard likely already filters it). Every former PREFERENCE float (Preview, QuickTime, Photo Booth, Activity Monitor, Stickies, Software Update, System Settings, System Information, Calculator, Finder copy/move/info dialogs, Archive Utility, 1Password, Bitwarden, KeePassXC) was REMOVED — a resizable+standard window of those apps now TILES; a non-resizable/non-standard one still floats structurally. To float an app back, append a {app, manage:off} rule here (the easy per-app escape hatch). Layering props (sticky, sub-layer, opacity, grid) are intentionally unsupported — Parcel's predicate only consults app/title/manage.
